profile.campus: CINECA Casalecchio di Reno Campus (historic HQ)
profile.address: Casalecchio di Reno, Bologna metropolitan area, Italy (near CINECA historic campus, Via Magnanelli)
profile.reading: This OSM point is tagged as the Leonardo supercomputer, one of the worlds most powerful, but its coordinates sit near Casalecchio di Reno, southwest of central Bologna, close to CINECAs older, historic campus at Via Magnanelli 6/3, rather than the confirmed Bologna Technopole site on Via Ferrarese where CINECAs own materials and independent reporting place Leonardo itself. CINECA, Italys leading public inter-university supercomputing consortium, operated its long standing flagship systems, including the earlier Marconi supercomputer, from the Casalecchio di Reno campus before Leonardo was installed at the newer Technopole site. Leonardo itself was funded through the European High Performance Computing Joint Undertaking, EuroHPC, in a 240 million euro project split evenly between the European Union and Italys Ministry of Education, University and Research, built on an Atos BullSequana XH2000 architecture with close to 14,000 Nvidia Ampere GPUs, delivering a peak theoretical performance of 250 petaflops and debuting at rank 4 on the TOP500 list of the worlds fastest supercomputers on November 24, 2022. Given the coordinate mismatch with Leonardos confirmed Technopole address, this entry treats this point as likely reflecting CINECAs separate Casalecchio di Reno campus, historically home to its earlier supercomputing generations, rather than asserting Leonardo itself sits at this specific location. Italian regional press reported CINECA inaugurating a supercomputer at its Casalecchio di Reno site in May 2017, consistent with the timeline of Marconi, the Cray/Lenovo based system that preceded Leonardo as CINECAs flagship national supercomputer before Leonardo took over that role at the Technopole in 2022. CINECA itself was founded in 1969 and headquartered at this Casalecchio di Reno campus, with additional locations in Milan, Rome, Naples, and Chieti, operating as a non-profit consortium of 69 Italian universities, 27 national public research centers, and Italys Ministry of Universities and Research and Ministry of Education, describing itself as the most powerful supercomputing center for scientific research in Italy. Beyond supercomputing, CINECA has since the late 1980s also provided administrative and ICT management services to Italian universities, and it consolidated much of the countrys academic computing capacity after merging with two other consortia, CILEA and Caspur.
profile.research_note: Corrected 2026-09-04: prior 2026-09-02 stale out-of-scope flag superseded, see Nasertic changelog entry seq 928/929 for the systematic bug explanation. This nodes coordinates (44.4863, 11.2598) do not match Leonardos confirmed Via Ferrarese/Bologna Technopole address; they sit closer to CINECAs older Casalecchio di Reno campus (Via Magnanelli 6/3). Flagged as a likely OSM naming/location mismatch rather than silently applying Leonardo specific facts (exact GPU count, InfiniBand config) to a location that does not match the supercomputers real site; general company and project context is given honestly instead.
